text.text_excerpt: Went to Ted Brennan's Decatur last night with a large group -- we had an excellent time. The food was wonderful and the service was impeccable. Our waiter (Ron) was very attentive and did a great job. For appetizers, we had escargot, oysters rockefeller and the decadent crepe. All three were fantastic and I would order them again. The decadent crepe was to die for -- we ended up ordering a second one. The turtle soup was the best I've had in New Orleans -- highly recommended. I had the Filet TMB. It was perfectly cooked and had a red wine reduction sauce. Very good. I really enjoyed it. For dessert we had bananas fosters, which they cooked in front of us -- a great show! We also tried the...

Only tried their happy hour, but it's a really great place. Part of the Brennan family chain of restaurants that dominate New Orleans. I think this is a newer place, opened up within the last month on Decatur Street. During happy hour select appetizers and drinks are half price, which is a great deal. I had the Legitimate Business Man cocktail (made with Old Forester 1897 whiskey!) and as far as I know unique to this establishment. It was strong and smooth, and a steal at only $6. They have other drinks too which are equally well valued. I also had the Turtle soup, which I've always wanted to try. It's a New Orleans staple, and served at quite a few places around town. I came here for a birthday brunch. The place is new and not on the "main drag," so it was pretty empty. I didn't mind though. The service was fantastic and what I expected from some of the "original" Brennan's staff. The eye-opener cocktails were enjoyed by all in our group. There is a prix-fixe brunch menu but most of our party just ordered entrées. There are some very classic Brennan's options as well as some newer ones. The gumbo was more like a creole stew - but VERY tomato based. That was one thing my grandparents (who make their own fantastic gumbo) weren't keen on.
